purpose: Stage 2 of the pre-Phase 7 screen: the concepts stage 1 could not express, tested with a rule simulator and an indicator library. A screen is not validation and decides nothing about profitability.

screen.note: The same 14 calendar days (10 trading days) as stage 1. Classification uses this window only.

context.note: Supplementary, about 11 weeks of the same spent development series. Once-a-day rules cannot reach 15 trades in 10 trading days; this run shows more trades for them. It does not classify anything and is not validation.

execution.bars: M5 bid candles (P7-VWAP: M1 in the screen window)
execution.costs: frozen Phase 5 cost model: candle spread (0.30 fallback), commission 3.50 USD/lot/side, slippage 0.05 USD per fill
fills: A rule decides at a bar's close; market orders fill at the next bar's open.
Stop-entry orders fill at their price, or at the open if the bar opens beyond it; buys trigger on the ask.
If a bar touches both the protective stop and the target, the stop counts first.
On the bar where a stop-entry fills, a touched protective stop counts as hit and a target does not.
Open positions are closed at the last close of the window.

conventions.r_without_stop: The source has no stop: R is a NOMINAL unit of 1.5 x ATR(14) on M15 at entry (GoldScalp's default ATR stop size). Marked nominal; USD results are always reported too.
conventions.unspecified_exits: Target not specified by a source: 2R. Time exit not specified: 240 minutes. Entry buffer not specified: 0.10 USD.
conventions.daily_rule_ports: Daily-bar rules without an intraday source are applied to M15 bars.
conventions.clock_times: Clock times are the source's own, in the source's timezone, daylight-saving aware (literal port).
conventions.no_tuning: No parameter is changed after a result is seen.

rules: Classification uses the screen window only.
WORTH FURTHER RESEARCH only if expectancy > 0, PF >= 1.1, still positive without its best day, positive with costs x2, and not negative when every order is delayed by one bar.
The one-bar delay replaces stage 1's M15-execution check: these rules are defined on fixed bar sizes and clock times, so re-running them on M15 bars would change the rules themselves.

baselines.name: Daily long 00:00 to 21:00 UTC (market drift after costs)

stage1_context.note: The three stage 1 candidates and the two archived benchmarks are re-run unchanged (bt@1 engine, M5) over the context window, in monthly pieces, for comparison only.

not_screened.why: MA type, stop and target are not specified, and M3 bars are not stored.

not_screened.concept: Cohen 2022 RSI / Keltner systems on gold futures
not_screened.why: The parameters are not given in the accessible abstract.
The stop is not stated in the accessible sources; the previous-day fade (P7-PDF) covers the same idea.
Needs traded volume across a stock universe.

candidates.name: London breakout of the Asian range (educational FX rules, clock-time range)
candidates.source: The Right Trader, 'London Breakout Strategy' (educational, FX majors)
candidates.original_rules: M15. Range = high/low of 00:00-07:00 UTC; skip if the range is below 0.25x or above 0.80x daily ATR(14). Entry 07:00-10:00 UTC on the first M15 close beyond the range. Stop: opposite side of the range. Target 1R. Exit at the first M15 close at or after 12:00 UTC. One trade per day.
candidates.implementation: As stated. Daily ATR(14) from trading days with the 17:00 New York rollover; entry at the next M5 open after the M15 close.
deviations: Spot XAUUSD instead of FX majors.

candidates.name: London breakout on gold (vendor rules, server-time range, OCO stop orders)
candidates.source: S. Pinjori, 'London Breakout on Gold: 3.7 Years of Backtests', MQL5 blog 2026 (promotional: sells an EA)
candidates.original_rules: XAUUSD. Range 03:00-08:00 broker server time. At 08:00 an OCO buy stop above the high and sell stop below the low with a small buffer (size not specified). Stop: opposite side of the range, capped at 0.6% of price. Target 2.5R; stop to break-even at +1.5R. Close at 21:00. One trade per day. Skip if the range is below 0.30% or above 1.60% of price.
candidates.implementation: As stated, with server time = New York time + 7 hours (the Vantage MT5 server clock). Buffer 0.10 USD.
deviations: The source does not name its brokers' server offset; the common New-York-close server clock was assumed.
Buffer not specified by the source: 0.10 USD.

candidates.name: Crabel stretch breakout after an NR4 day
candidates.source: T. Crabel 1990 (book, via secondary summaries); stretch formula per nexusfi; Oxford Capital 'Narrow Range'
candidates.original_rules: Stretch = 10-day SMA of min(High-Open, Open-Low). Buy stop at Open + Stretch, sell stop at Open - Stretch; the first fill is the position and the other order becomes the protective stop. Trade the day after an NR4/NR7 day. Crabel's own exits: not verified (classic ORB exits at the close).
candidates.implementation: Trading day = 17:00 New York rollover; Open = the first M5 open of the day. Orders are placed at the close of the day's first M5 bar and stay until 5 minutes before the rollover, when any position is closed. NR4 = the previous day's range is the smallest of the last 4 days (NR7 days are a subset).
deviations: Exit at the end of the trading day (not verified in the source).
Orders start one M5 bar after the open.

candidates.name: 5-minute opening-range breakout in the first candle's direction
candidates.source: Zarattini & Aziz, 'Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable?', SSRN 4416622 (2023); QQQ
candidates.original_rules: First 5-minute bar 09:30-09:35 ET: long if it closed up, short if down, no trade on a doji. Enter at the 09:35 open. Stop: the first bar's low (long) or high (short). Target 10R, otherwise exit at 16:00.
candidates.implementation: As stated, with the paper's clock times unchanged (literal port to spot gold).
deviations: Gold has no 09:30 opening auction; the paper's clock was kept unchanged.

candidates.name: Noise-area intraday momentum (base version)
candidates.source: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon, 'Beat the Market', SSRN 2024/25; SPY
candidates.original_rules: sigma(HH:MM) = 14-day average of |Close(HH:MM)/Open(09:30) - 1|. Upper = max(Open, previous close) x (1+sigma), lower = min(Open, previous close) x (1-sigma). Checked at HH:00 and HH:30: long above the upper band, short below the lower. Exit on a cross of the opposite band (then reverse) or at 16:00.
candidates.implementation: As stated (base version without the VWAP stop), with the paper's clock unchanged. Previous close = the price at 16:00 New York the previous session.
deviations: Gold trades around the clock; the 09:30-16:00 New York session was kept as the 'day'.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: First-half-hour to last-half-hour intraday momentum
candidates.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou, Journal of Financial Economics 2018; SPY
candidates.original_rules: r1 = return from the previous 16:00 close to 10:00 ET. At 15:30 go long if r1 > 0, short otherwise. Close at 16:00.
candidates.implementation: As stated, with the paper's clock unchanged.
deviations: No stop in the source: nominal R.
No trade when r1 is exactly zero.

candidates.name: VWAP trend (tick-volume proxy)
candidates.source: Zarattini & Aziz, 'VWAP: The Holy Grail for Day Trading Systems', SSRN 4631351 (2023); QQQ
candidates.original_rules: Session VWAP from the open on 1-minute bars. Long when the 1-minute close is above VWAP, short when below; flip on each cross; flat before the close.
candidates.implementation: As stated on M1 bars in the screen window, with broker TICK volume as the volume (spot gold has no traded volume).
deviations: Tick volume is a proxy, not traded volume: this is not the source's indicator.
The context run uses M5 bars (M1 history starts on 28 September 2026).
No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: Turtle Soup Plus One (failed 20-bar breakout), M15 port
candidates.source: Connors & Raschke, 'Street Smarts' (1995), via secondary summaries
candidates.original_rules: Daily bars. A new 20-day low with the previous 20-day low at least 4 sessions old; 'Plus One': the setup bar closes at or below the prior low and the entry is the next day with a buy stop at the prior 20-day low. Stop just below the setup low. Target and time exit not specified. Sells mirrored.
candidates.implementation: The Plus One rules on M15 bars: buy stop at the prior 20-bar low + 0.10 for the next M15 bar only; stop 0.10 below the setup bar's low.
deviations: Daily-bar rules applied to M15 bars: an untested extrapolation.
Target and time exit not specified: 2R and 240 minutes.
The source's trailing stop is not specified and was not used.

candidates.name: RSI(2) extreme mean reversion on M30
candidates.source: Connors & Alvarez 2008 (book, via StockCharts ChartSchool); intraday version Z.K. Chen, MQL5 article 2025
candidates.original_rules: Long above the 200 SMA when RSI(2) <= 5; short below it when RSI(2) >= 95. Exit longs on a close above the 5 SMA (shorts: below). Chen's M30 version adds a 0.15% stop.
candidates.implementation: As stated on M30 bars with the 0.15% stop; entries and exits at the next M5 open after the M30 close.
deviations: US500 / daily-stock rules applied to gold.

candidates.name: Bollinger %b mean reversion, M15 port
candidates.source: Connors & Alvarez (book, via Quantified Strategies and Oxford Capital)
candidates.original_rules: Long: close above the 200 SMA and %b below 0.2 for 3 consecutive bars; exit when %b closes above 0.8. Oxford Capital adds a mirrored short.
candidates.implementation: As stated on M15 bars with the mirrored short; BB(20,2).
deviations: Daily ETF rules applied to M15 gold bars.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: TTM squeeze breakout, M15 port
candidates.source: J. Carter, 'Mastering the Trade' (via StockCharts ChartSchool 'TTM Squeeze')
candidates.original_rules: Squeeze on while BB(20,2) is inside KC(20, 1.5 ATR); it fires when the bands move back outside. Long if the momentum histogram is above zero and rising, short if below zero and falling. Exit after 2 consecutive bars of the new histogram colour. Stop not specified.
candidates.implementation: As stated on M15 bars. Momentum = 20-bar linear-regression value of close - ((highest high + lowest low)/2 + SMA)/2; Keltner = SMA(20) +/- 1.5 x average true range(20).
deviations: The histogram formula differs between platforms; the common one was used.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: 5-minute SMA crossover on gold: the paper's best rule SMA(44, 332)
candidates.source: Urquhart, Batten, Lucey, McGroarty & Peat, SSRN 2652637 (2015); 5-minute spot gold 2008-2014
candidates.original_rules: Long when MA(short) is above MA(long), short when below; always in the market. Standard rules (1,50), (1,100), (1,150), (1,200) are not profitable; the best in-sample SMA rule is (44, 332). No costs in the paper.
candidates.implementation: SMA(44) vs SMA(332) on M5 closes, flipping at the next open.
deviations: No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: Gold time-of-day: long 11:00 to 02:00, short 02:00 to 11:00 New York
candidates.source: Donati & Jung, 'Gold Price Dynamics Around the Clock', MSc thesis, Copenhagen Business School 2019; COMEX gold
candidates.original_rules: Long: buy at 11:00, sell at 02:00 the next day (New York time). Short: short at 02:00, cover at 11:00. Combo: both. No stops.
candidates.implementation: The combo, as stated; both legs are also reported separately.
deviations: Spot XAUUSD instead of COMEX futures.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: Short gold in the half hour before the London fixes
candidates.source: Donati & Jung 2019 (same thesis); context: Caminschi & Heaney, Journal of Futures Markets 2014
candidates.original_rules: Short 05:05-05:35 and 09:35-10:05 New York time (around the AM and PM London fixes). No stops.
candidates.implementation: As stated, in New York time.
deviations: London and New York change clocks on different dates; the thesis's New York times were kept.
No stop in the source: nominal R.

candidates.name: EMA trend-pullback scalp with the source's 8/34 EMAs
candidates.source: J. Stanley (DailyFX), 'Short-term momentum scalping in the forex market', IG (broker education)
candidates.original_rules: H1: 8 EMA above the 34 EMA with price above both (mirror for shorts). M5: after a pullback to or through the 8 EMA, enter when trend-side momentum comes back. Stop beyond the previous swing. Target not specified.
candidates.implementation: Pullback = an M5 close at or below the M5 8 EMA while the H1 trend is up; entry = the first later M5 close back above it. Stop 0.10 below the lowest low of the pullback. Mirror for shorts.
deviations: 'Momentum comes back' is discretionary in the source; the first close back beyond the 8 EMA was used.
Target and time exit not specified: 2R and 240 minutes.
